question: The Directive establishing the European Disability Card and the European Parking Card for persons with disabilities lays down a clear timeline (notification of contact points by June 2025, transposition by June 2027 and application from June 2028), but some crucial delegated acts are still in the process of being adopted.

In the meantime, national card holders are met with refusals to recognise their cards and are given unjustified fines in other Member States. Can the EU ensure that the deadline is met and that there is a smooth transition of rights for persons with disabilities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.10.2026) In line with Directive (EU) 2024/28411, persons with disabilities in the EU will be able to benefit from the European Disability Card (EDC) and the European Parking Card for persons with disabilities (EPC) as from 5 June 2028.

The Commission supports the Member States in the transposition of the Directive through the organisation of discussions and provision of guidance. The Commission also takes steps to facilitate and enable the application of the Directive.

On 1 July 2026, the Commission adopted the Commission Delegated Regulation supplementing the Directive as regards setting the QR code on the physical version of the EDC and setting the QR code and establishing common technical specifications that ensure the security of the physical version of the EPC, as well as interoperability matters2.

The act is currently under scrutiny by the European Parliament and the Council. The Commission is currently also preparing an implementing act concerning the digital versions of the cards pursuant to Article 9 of Directive (EU) 2024/2841.
